feature: UX critique fixes, stage C: a 13 px type floor, a skills home that opens readable and a gated root suite, GitHub said once, chart words with their meaning; one request for the rail, the cards and Triage with Triage's all-time view, the project spend served, reuse evidence and redacted contradictory results served, and run controls to retry every failed check and relaunch a dead lane

scenarios.description: At 1440x900 and at 390x844, on the Projects cards, a seeded project page with its step chart, Triage, a seeded feature page, a seeded run page (its dock open and its Sessions table) and a seeded review node page: every visible element that holds its own non-empty text, outside the run stage's zoomed graph, has a computed font-size of at least 13 px at 1440 and at least 14 px at 390, except an element whose computed text-transform is uppercase, which is at least 11 px at both widths; every visible <code> inside the Projects shell is at least 13 px at 1440; no page is wider than the window at either width.

On the Projects page and the project pages of seeded projects at 1440x900: the card of the seeded project whose GitHub status is not_github reads 'no GitHub remote' in its foot and never 'GitHub not read'; its project page says 'no GitHub remote' exactly once, in the GitHub column's one line, and renders no Pull requests or Issues card; with the overview answered by page.route in both phases with a project whose status is unavailable (reason 'gh is not installed'), its project page says 'GitHub not read: gh is not installed' exactly once and renders no Pull requests or Issues card repeating it; a project whose GitHub was read keeps its pull request and issue counts; the Projects page meta line says 'GitHub read <time>' when any project was read, and says nothing about GitHub when no project has a GitHub remote; no text anywhere reads 'GitHub not read: not a GitHub remote'.

On a seeded project page whose features ended at several steps, at 1440x900: every non-empty cell of the 'ended here' row reads '<n> ended at <phase>' with the full phase name of its column, or '<n> landed' under Integrate, is not cut (its scrollWidth does not exceed its clientWidth) and has an accessible name equal to its text; the row label 'ended here' stays; the axis shows the eight full phase names; with the chart's container under 640 px wide (a run selected at 1024x900, or the narrowest desktop width at which the short forms show), every short axis label is explained by a visible legend under the chart that names its phase, and no axis label contains '…'; the Verify count stays centred under its column at 1440 and 1100 px. At that narrow desktop container width the test also asserts every legend entry visible inside the chart container with its full name, not clipped (scrollWidth <= clientWidth), with no ellipsis and no sideways scroll (wrapping allowed).

The skills home at 1440x900 opens in the graph, without a click, with the Pi and Claude sources expanded exactly one level: each location of the suite's generated sources.json shows as a node with its counts, named in the graph's accessible names, and lies inside the graph canvas with no scroll or zoom change; no folder or file node shows; no file-operation button is shown until a source, location, folder or file is selected, and then only the operations that apply to the selection are shown, none disabled; Reset returns to the opened-one-level view and announces 'Reset: showing the Pi and Claude sources and their locations.'; Outline shows the same expansion and selection and returns to the graph unchanged; at 360x640 the first view is the same, Refresh, Zoom in, Zoom out, Fit, Reset and Outline are inside the viewport in that order, and the page does not scroll sideways.

In both phases with page.clock installed at a fixed time, at 1440x900: on Triage and on the Projects cards, across one poll interval the page issues exactly one request to /api/dispatch/runs (with a since parameter) and one to /api/dispatch/projects, and none to /api/projects/

/workflows or to a workflow's run-list route; on a project page the only run-list requests are that project's own first-page reads of its features; Triage's sections, counts and rows and the rail's badges are the same as stage A's and B's scenarios assert for the same seeds; while a poll is in flight the rows stay on screen and no 'reading' wording returns; with /api/dispatch/runs answered by page.route with no running or waiting run, the next read comes 60 s after the last one and none at 15 s, and an answer holding a running run brings the next read back to 15 s; between two on-time 60 s polls Triage's live status never reads 'Not updating'; a home read answered with an error keeps the last rows and shows the not-read wording with its reason.

On Triage at 1440x900 with page.clock installed at a fixed time and /api/dispatch/runs/all answered as two pages by page.route in both phases (the first with a next_cursor): the date control offers exactly 'Any date', 'Today', '7 days' and 'All time'; choosing 'All time' issues one request per page and no other, shows 'Reading older runs… (<n> read)' while reading, then replaces the state sections with one All runs list (all-runs; Pinned stays above it) holding every run read exactly once, including a run finished more than 7 days ago that no section shows; the status, stopped-at and text controls filter it; the scope line reads '<k> of <n> runs · every project, all loaded'; when the second page answers with an error, 'The next page of runs' panel shows Retry, the rows read and the filters stay and the scope line reads '<k> of <n> runs · every project · Load more runs', never 'all loaded'; Retry requests only the second page again, and once it answers the scope line reads '<k> of <n> runs · every project, all loaded'; when a page lists an unreadable workflow, Triage's Attention section (lists-errors) names that workflow as not read; choosing 'Any date' restores the sections with no request; date=all is in the URL and survives opening a run and Back, and a reload; the tab title's '(n)', the rail badges and the Pinned section do not change with the choice.

In both phases, at 1440x900 on seeded project pages: a project whose runs' exports record Claude costs shows in its figures '$<x> Claude spend · <k> of <n> runs priced', x the sum of the seeded costs.total_usd to the cent, k the runs with a recorded total and n every run of the project's readable workflows; no spend figure shows before the overview read settles; a seeded project with no recorded cost reads 'no Claude spend recorded'; no project header reads 'spend not recorded'; the figures' other entries are unchanged.

In the candidate phase, on the candidate node page of the seeded run whose candidate packet for a lane reuses that lane's worker packet of attempt 1: the reuse list (reuse-list) reads 'Attempt <a> reused the result of attempt 1' with the event's message; the candidate node page of a seeded run without reuse shows no reuse list; in the worker phase the mocked reuse event on verify_ui still renders 'Attempt 2 reused the result of attempt 1'.

With run controls paired, in both phases: the Controls list of a seeded run holds 14 controls; on a seeded stopped automatic run where two worker lanes' verify steps failed, 'Retry all failed checks' is available, its command names 'retry' with '--phase worker --all-failed', and confirming it records one completed command whose output lists both lanes; on the seeded run with one failed lane it is unavailable with a reason; on a seeded run whose lane launch needs reconciliation and left no live session, 'Relaunch a lane' is available with that lane as its only choice, its dialog shows the dry run's first line 'relaunch <lane>: allowed' before Confirm is enabled, and a confirmed relaunch records 'Relaunched <lane> once' and the two continuation lines, after which Reconcile is offered; with the controller's dry run refusing ('relaunch <lane>: refused: …'), the dialog shows that line verbatim and Confirm stays disabled.
